Then Telemachus got into the chariot, while Pacistratus gathered up the reins and took
He lashed the horses on, and they flew forward nothing loth into the open country, leaving
the high citadel of pilos behind them.
All that day did they travel, swaying the yoke upon their necks till the sun went down
and darkness was over all the land.
Then they reached Faerie where Diocles lived, who was son to Ordolotchus and grandson to
Here they passed the night, and Diocles entertained them hospitably.
When the child of morning, Rosy-fingered Dawn, appeared, they again yoked their horses and
drove out through the gateway under the echoing gatehouse.
Pacistratus lashed the horses on, and they flew forward nothing loth.
Presently they came to the cornlands of the open country, and in the course of time completed
their journey, so well did their steeds take them.
